---
title: "Spec cookbook"
---

Copy-paste starting points for the dataset layouts we actually encounter.
Every pattern here comes from a real dataset in the project, but the study names and filenames are fictional.
Each pattern shows the folder layout (expand the callout) and the `dataset.yaml` that reads it; field meanings are in [The dataset.yaml spec](dataset-yaml.qmd).

## 1. One data file, nothing else

The simplest possible spec.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Folder layout

```text
BPIPD-9999 - Example Cohort Study/
└── data.sav
```
:::

```yaml
dataset_id: "9999"
dataset_name: "Example Cohort Study"
status: "in_progress"

resources:
  - name: "data"
    role: "data"
    glob: "data.sav"
    reader: "spss"
```

## 2. Several data files, joined later in the tidier

One resource per file, each with its own name.
The spec only *reads* the files — combining them (joins, binds) happens in the [tidy script](tidy-scripts.qmd).

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Folder layout

```text
BPIPD-9999 - Example Cohort Study/
├── demographics.xlsx
├── questionnaire.xlsx
└── motor_skills.xlsx
```
:::

```yaml
resources:
  - name: "demographics"
    role: "data"
    glob: "demographics.xlsx"
    reader: "excel"
    sheet: "Data"
  - name: "questionnaire"
    role: "data"
    glob: "questionnaire.xlsx"
    reader: "excel"
    sheet: "Data"
  - name: "motor_skills"
    role: "data"
    glob: "motor_skills.xlsx"
    reader: "excel"
    sheet: "Data"
```

The tidier then accesses `raw_dataset$data$demographics`, `raw_dataset$data$questionnaire`, and so on.

## 3. Waves in a flat folder (wave in the filename)

All files sit at the dataset root; the wave is encoded in each filename.
Use `wave_dir: "."` and wave-specific resource names.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Folder layout

```text
BPIPD-9999 - Example Cohort Study/
├── survey_2010.csv
├── survey_2010_codebook.pdf
├── survey_2014.csv
└── survey_2014_codebook.pdf
```
:::

```yaml
waves:
  - wave: "2010"
    label: "2010"
    wave_dir: "."
    resources:
      - name: "data_2010"
        role: "data"
        glob: "survey_2010.csv"
        reader: "csv"
      - name: "codebook_2010"
        role: "codebook"
        glob: "survey_2010_codebook.pdf"
  - wave: "2014"
    label: "2014"
    wave_dir: "."
    resources:
      - name: "data_2014"
        role: "data"
        glob: "survey_2014.csv"
        reader: "csv"
      - name: "codebook_2014"
        role: "codebook"
        glob: "survey_2014_codebook.pdf"
```

Every data table gets `.wave` and `.wave_label` columns, and the tidier typically `bind_rows()`s the waves together.

## 4. Waves in per-wave subfolders

Each wave has its own directory: point `wave_dir` at it, and globs become relative to that directory.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Folder layout

```text
BPIPD-9999 - Example Cohort Study/
├── 2016 Survey Files/
│   ├── survey_2016.csv
│   └── codebook_2016.pdf
└── 2017 Survey Files/
    ├── survey_2017.csv
    └── codebook_2017.pdf
```
:::

```yaml
waves:
  - wave: "2016"
    label: "2016"
    wave_dir: "2016 Survey Files"
    resources:
      - name: "data_2016"
        role: "data"
        glob: "survey_2016.csv"
        reader: "csv"
  - wave: "2017"
    label: "2017"
    wave_dir: "2017 Survey Files"
    resources:
      - name: "data_2017"
        role: "data"
        glob: "survey_2017.csv"
        reader: "csv"
```

An equally valid alternative is to keep `wave_dir: "."` and put the folder in the glob (`glob: "2016 Survey Files/survey_2016.csv"`).
Pick one style per file and stay consistent.

## 5. Two logical waves sharing one folder

Waves do not have to map one-to-one onto folders.
Here two instruments collected in the same year live in the same directory but are treated as separate waves:

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Folder layout

```text
BPIPD-9999 - Example Cohort Study/
└── 2007/
    ├── parent_survey.dta
    └── child_assessment.dta
```
:::

```yaml
waves:
  - wave: "2007_parent"
    label: "2007 Parent Survey"
    wave_dir: "2007"
    resources:
      - name: "data_2007_parent"
        role: "data"
        glob: "parent_survey.dta"
        reader: "stata"
  - wave: "2007_child"
    label: "2007 Child Assessment"
    wave_dir: "2007"
    resources:
      - name: "data_2007_child"
        role: "data"
        glob: "child_assessment.dta"
        reader: "stata"
```

## 6. Many similar files via a wildcard

When a folder holds many files of the same kind, one resource with a wildcard reads them all.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Folder layout

```text
BPIPD-9999 - Example Cohort Study/
└── stata/
    └── annual/
        ├── survey_1994.dta
        ├── survey_1995.dta
        ├── ...
        └── survey_2008.dta
```
:::

```yaml
resources:
  - name: "annual_surveys"
    role: "data"
    glob: "stata/annual/*.dta"
    reader: "stata"
```

Each matched file becomes its own table named `annual_surveys__1`, `annual_surveys__2`, … in `raw_dataset$data` (in file-listing order).
Prefer explicitly named resources when there are only a few files or when they play different roles in the tidier — `data$annual_surveys__3` is much less self-documenting than `data$youth_questionnaire`.

## 7. Grouping a few files in one resource

For a handful of files that share a role, either a YAML list or brace notation works.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Folder layout

```text
BPIPD-9999 - Example Cohort Study/
├── sweep1/
│   ├── child_interview.sav
│   └── parent_interview.sav
└── docs/
    ├── technical_report.pdf
    └── user_guide.pdf
```
:::

```yaml
resources:
  - name: "interviews"
    role: "data"
    glob:
      - "sweep1/child_interview.sav"
      - "sweep1/parent_interview.sav"
    reader: "spss"
  - name: "documentation"
    role: "docs"
    glob: "docs/{technical_report.pdf,user_guide.pdf}"
```

As with wildcards, multiple matches become `interviews__1`, `interviews__2`, …

## 8. Codebooks and documentation

Codebooks and docs are recorded so we know they exist, but only `data` resources are read into R.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Folder layout

```text
BPIPD-9999 - Example Cohort Study/
├── survey.xlsx
├── survey_dictionary.xlsx
└── docs/
    ├── questionnaire.pdf
    └── technical_report.pdf
```
:::

```yaml
resources:
  - name: "data"
    role: "data"
    glob: "survey.xlsx"
    reader: "excel"
    sheet: "Data"
  - name: "data_dictionary"
    role: "codebook"
    glob: "survey_dictionary.xlsx"
  - name: "documentation"
    role: "docs"
    glob: "docs/{questionnaire.pdf,technical_report.pdf}"
```

A single workbook sometimes holds the data on one sheet and the codebook on another — declare the data sheet as the `data` resource and list the same file again as a `codebook` resource for the record.

## 9. Readers with extra keys

Most readers need nothing beyond `reader:`.
Three take extra keys:

```yaml
resources:
  # Excel: sheet (name or number), optionally a cell range
  - name: "survey"
    role: "data"
    glob: "survey.xlsx"
    reader: "excel"
    sheet: "Data"
    range: "A1:H200"

  # Microsoft Access: which table to read
  # (optional when the file has exactly one table — if you omit it and
  # there are several, the error message lists the available tables)
  - name: "assessments"
    role: "data"
    glob: "study_database.mdb"
    reader: "mdb"
    table: "Assessments"

  # .rda: which object to extract
  # (optional when the file holds exactly one object)
  - name: "cohort"
    role: "data"
    glob: "cohort_2012.rda"
    reader: "rda"
    object: "cohort_data"
```

## 10. Dataset-wide files alongside waves

When a codebook or metadata file covers the whole study, keep it in a top-level `resources` list next to the `waves`:

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Folder layout

```text
BPIPD-9999 - Example Cohort Study/
├── codebook_all_waves.pdf
├── sweep1_data.sav
└── sweep2_data.sav
```
:::

```yaml
resources:
  - name: "study_codebook"
    role: "codebook"
    glob: "codebook_all_waves.pdf"

waves:
  - wave: "sweep_1"
    label: "sweep_1"
    wave_dir: "."
    resources:
      - name: "data_sweep_1"
        role: "data"
        glob: "sweep1_data.sav"
        reader: "spss"
  - wave: "sweep_2"
    label: "sweep_2"
    wave_dir: "."
    resources:
      - name: "data_sweep_2"
        role: "data"
        glob: "sweep2_data.sav"
        reader: "spss"
```
